transcript: Birdie
Hi! I help businesses figure out exactly what they need from a chatbot. Before we start — what's your name?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh hello love! Yes, sorry, I'm just out here with a bucket of feed in one hand, typing with the other, so forgive me if this comes out a bit wonky — it's Roz. Rosalind Fenwick, but nobody's called me Rosalind since my Aunt Pat's funeral, and even then only because the vicar read it off the order of service and got it wrong anyway, said "Rosalinde" like I was foreign or something, bless him.

Anyway — Roz. I run The Shaggy Dog House, it's just out the back of my cottage in Nether Compton, converted stable block, been going eleven years now. Started it after my knee went and I couldn't do the school run job anymore, funny how these things work out isn't it. What was it you needed, sorry, I do go on!
Birdie

Lovely to meet you, Roz — and no apologies needed, I love that you're multitasking with a feed bucket! The Shaggy Dog House sounds like a lovely spot. So I get the full picture — is it dog grooming, boarding, daycare, or a bit of everything?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Bit of everything really, well — grooming and boarding, not daycare as such, though funny you ask because I did have a woman once, oh must've been 2015 or so, ask if I'd have her spaniel just for the day while she went to a wedding, and I said well I'm not really set up for that but go on then, and honestly that dog howled the whole six hours, poor thing, made me feel dreadful. Never did it again after that, not properly anyway, though I suppose I do bend the rules now and then for the regulars.

But yes — grooming, that's washes and full grooms, nails, the lot, and I've got my niece Tilly who does that with me Thursdays and Fridays, lovely girl, bit of a whizz with the poodle crosses. And then boarding, I've got three runs out in the stable block, dogs get two walks a day out round the field behind us, weather permitting, though it's been that muddy lately I've had to keep them to the lane instead, my wellies have never seen the like.

Sorry — grooming and boarding, that's your answer! I do wander.
Birdie

That all makes sense, Roz — grooming and boarding, no daycare unless it's a regular you're bending the rules for! Let's start with grooming — what do you typically charge for a wash, a full groom, and nails, and roughly how long does each take?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh now, pricing — right, let me think, though I should say the timing bit's a bit of a guess because it really does depend on the dog, I had a Bernese in once took nearly three hours because he just would not stand still on the table, kept sitting down like a big sulky teenager, and Tilly ended up laughing so hard she had to go outside.

But basics — wash and brush is £25 for a small dog, £35 medium, £45 if it's a big one or a double coat, all that undercoat business, terrible for the hoover after. Full groom, so that's the wash plus the cut, nails and ears done properly, that's £40, £55, £70 same sizes. Nails on their own if that's all they need, just £8, quick job, dog's usually more upset about it than it needs to be, they do fuss.

Oh and I do a puppy session too, just get them used to the table and the dryer noise, that's £15 though half the time I forget to even charge for it, terrible business woman really, Derek at the feed shop always tells me off about it.

Time-wise — wash and brush maybe an hour, hour and a bit, full groom more like two hours, two and a half if they're wriggly. Sorry, was that what you needed?
Birdie
Brilliant, that's really clear, thank you Roz. Now for boarding — what do you charge per night (or per day), and does it vary by dog size at all?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh boarding, no it's not size-based like the grooming, flat rate whatever they are, though I did once have a Great Dane in — lovely soppy thing called Bruno, ate more than my Terry does and he's a grown man — and I did think, I should really charge more for you, love, but I never did, didn't have the heart, he used to lean on you like a wardrobe falling over, very affectionate.

But no — it's £28 a night per dog, that includes the two walks, morning and teatime, round the field or the lane depending how mucky it's got, and if it's a two-dog household, same family sort of thing, I knock £5 off the second dog's night, seems only fair really since they're often happier sharing anyway, less howling in the night.

So £28 a night, £23 for the second one if there's two of them. That's your answer, sorry, go on!
Birdie

Got it, flat £28 a night, £23 for a second dog from the same family — lovely and simple. Now, how many dogs can you actually board at once with the three runs, and do you ever get fully booked, like at holiday times?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh yes, three runs is all I've got, so three dogs is really my limit — well, unless it's two from the same family who don't mind sharing a run, which I do sometimes do, saves space and they're often happier together anyway like I said with the howling business. Though — and I really ought to sort this out, it's been on my list forever — I've never actually rung the insurance people to check whether I'm covered properly having two unrelated dogs share a run, I just assumed I would be, but "assumed" isn't much good if something went wrong, is it. Terry keeps telling me to just ring them, and I keep saying yes yes, and then Derek at the feed shop needs seeing to about an order or the guttering starts up again, and it never happens.

But to answer you properly — yes, we do get fully booked, especially round the school holidays, Easter and summer especially, people book Cornwall and can't take the dog, understandably. Half term's bad too. Honestly though, love, if you asked me right now how many spaces I've got free this coming week I couldn't tell you off the top of my head, I'd have to walk out to the stable block and actually look at the board, and I say I'll do that most days and then don't, terrible isn't it. Was there something specific you needed to know, like a date?
Birdie

That's really useful, Roz — sounds like the board out in the stable block is your real record of who's in when. Since there's no digital calendar, how would you want the bot to handle availability questions — should it just tell people to ring or message you to check, rather than guessing a yes or no?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh yes, that'd be sensible, wouldn't it — better than the bot promising someone a space and then me having to ring back all apologetic saying sorry love, we're chock full, I forgot to look at the board again. So yes, tell them to ring or message and I'll pop out and check the actual board, don't have it guess, because honestly even I get it wrong sometimes, I thought I had a run free for a lady's cocker spaniel back in April and then remembered Bruno the Great Dane's owners had already booked it for that same week, big mix up, lots of apologising involved.

So — bot says something like "let me check with Roz and get back to you" sort of thing, that'd be perfect. Especially around the school holidays like I said, Easter and summer, people do need telling straight rather than left hanging, I know that much even if I'm hopeless with the board itself.

Was there more you needed on that, or shall I tell you about the vaccination business next, because that's important too — can't have dogs boarding without their kennel cough jab up to date, learned that one the hard way an' all!
Birdie

Perfect, that's a sensible way to handle it. Yes, please tell me about the vaccination rule — what exactly do dogs need to be up to date on before boarding, and is that the same for grooming visits too?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh yes, right — kennel cough, that's the big one for boarding, has to be up to date within the last twelve months, and I do actually ask for proof, a little vaccination card or the vet printout, whatever they've got. Learned that one the hard way because years back — ooh, must've been 2018, maybe 2019 — I had a lady bring her westie in, lovely little dog, but no jab, hadn't even thought about it, and within about four days I had two others coughing away like a pair of old men down the pub, terrible racket at night, and I felt sick about it, ringing the other owners up all apologetic. So now I don't budge on that one, boarding needs the kennel cough jab, current, no exceptions, doesn't matter how sweet the dog is.

Grooming's a different thing though — that's not about the kennel cough, that's flea treatment I'm meant to check for, up to date flea stuff before I'll do a full groom, because obviously you don't want fleas jumping ship into the dryer and then onto the next dog. I am meant to be strict about that one an' all, but if I'm honest, love, I do let it slide sometimes for the regulars, people I've known years, I just think well I know your dog, I'm sure it's fine — probably shouldn't admit that to you really, should I!

But there's your answer — kennel cough for boarding, flea treatment for grooming, two different things.
Birdie
Good to know, and totally understandable about the regulars! Now let's talk money — how do customers usually pay you, cash, card, bank transfer — and does that work smoothly, or are there hiccups?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh payment — right, well, mostly it's cash still if I'm honest, lot of my regulars just hand me an envelope or shove a tenner in my apron pocket when they drop off, very old-fashioned I know. But I did get one of them little card machines a couple of years back, Tilly badgered me into it actually, said "Auntie Roz you can't keep asking people if they've got the right change," and she was right, because I did have an awful moment with a gentleman once, lovely man, brought his lurcher in for a full groom, and neither of us had change for a fifty, ended up he had to nip to the shop and buy a paper he didn't even want just to break the note, daft really.

So now it's cash or the card machine, and some of the boarding families do bank transfer, especially if they're booking ahead for a week or two, easier for them to just do it online before they even come. Works alright mostly — machine does go a bit funny sometimes if the signal's bad out in the stable block, I've had to walk halfway up the garden holding it in the air like an idiot trying to get a bar of signal, very glamorous.

Oh and the deposit thing, I should say — technically if someone cancels under 24 hours they're meant to forfeit a tenner deposit, but truth is I almost never actually charge it, I feel too guilty, unless it's someone taking the mick regularly, which does happen now and again!

Was that what you needed, love?
Birdie

That's really helpful, thank you. Now, what days and hours are you actually open for drop-offs and pick-ups, and is there an address or area you'd want the bot to give people (like Nether Compton, or a fuller address)?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh hours, yes — officially it's Tuesday to Saturday, nine till four, that's what I'd want on the sign if I ever got round to sorting a proper sign, mine's gone all faded, Terry keeps saying he'll repaint it and two summers later, still hasn't, bless him, he's better with the guttering than a paintbrush.

But truth be told, love, I'm often out there in the stable block from about half seven feeding the boarders and mucking out, so if someone turns up early or messages early I'm usually about and happy to chat, doesn't bother me. Closed Sundays and Mondays "in theory" is how I'd put it, because I have definitely answered messages of a Sunday morning in my dressing gown with a cup of tea, terrible discipline really. Tilly's only in Thursdays and Fridays for the grooming side, mind, so if it's specifically a grooming appointment they're after, best steer them to those two days, though I can sometimes do a wash myself other days if I'm not run off my feet.

As for where we are — it's Nether Compton, the cottage with the converted stable block out back, I'm on... oh gosh, hang on, it's Mill Lane, yes, Mill Lane, Nether Compton, though half the delivery drivers still end up at the wrong end by the church, there's no proper sign at the turning, another thing on Terry's list! I'd say give people the village and Mill Lane and tell them to ring if they get lost, because postcodes and them country lanes don't always agree with each other, satnav's sent people right into the Hendersons' farmyard before now, chickens everywhere, quite a to-do.

Was that everything on hours, or did you want the puppy sessions bit too?
Birdie

That's great, thank you — I've got the hours and location noted, including that tricky turning! Yes, let's do the puppy sessions bit too, but first — when the bot can't answer something or a customer needs a real person, what number or way should it point them to reach you (or Terry/Tilly), and what should it say if that's out of hours?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh, right, contact — well, I suppose it'd just be my mobile, same one I'm typing on now actually, I don't have a proper separate business line or anything fancy like that, never got round to it, Terry did suggest one of them WhatsApp business things a while back but I never worked out how to set it up properly, kept pressing the wrong button and it sent Sandra down the road a picture of my compost bin instead of the price list, don't ask.

So yes — my mobile, people can ring or text, and I do answer most of the time, even out of hours if I'm honest, like I say I've replied Sunday mornings in my dressing gown more than once. If I genuinely don't see it — and that does happen if I'm elbow deep in a poodle or out on the lane with the boarders — I'd want the bot to just say something like "Roz will get back to you as soon as she can, she's probably got her hands full of dog!" Don't put Tilly's number on there mind, she's only in for the grooming Thursdays and Fridays and she'd have my life if people started ringing her about boarding, she's got enough on with college stuff and this Bristol business she keeps hinting at.

Oh — and don't put Terry's number either, whatever you do, man cannot work a mobile phone to save his life, he'd answer it upside down.

Right, puppy sessions — where was I...
Birdie

That's really clear, thank you Roz — mobile only, no Tilly or Terry, and that lovely 'hands full of dog' line for when you're mid-poodle. Go on then, tell me about the puppy sessions — anything more to add beyond the £15 and getting them used to the table and dryer?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh yes, puppy sessions — well, it's mostly just what I said, get them up on the table, little clip on so they can't wriggle off, run the dryer for a bit even if there's nothing to dry, just so the noise isn't a big shock the first time they come in for a proper groom. I do a bit of nail handling too, just touching their paws, getting them used to that, because that's half the battle with grooming, honestly, it's not the cutting that upsets them, it's just not being used to being handled and fussed over in that way.

Had a cockapoo pup in not long back, little thing called Biscuit, couldn't have been more than twelve weeks, and he was shaking like a leaf to start with, bless him, but by the end he was falling asleep on the table with the dryer going, mum couldn't believe it when she came to pick him up. That's really the whole point of it, so by the time they're old enough for a proper wash or groom they're not petrified.

It's fifteen pound, like I said, for about twenty minutes, half hour if they're a nervous one and need coaxing along slow. And yes — I do forget to charge for it more than I should, Derek's told me off about it more than once, "you're not a charity, Roz," he says, and I say I know, I know, and then some little pup gives me a look and I just think, oh go on then, no charge today.

Anyway — that's puppy sessions! What else did you need, love?
Birdie

Aw, Biscuit sounds like a little star! Right, switching gears a bit — where do customers usually reach you now: is it phone calls and texts mostly, or do you get messages on WhatsApp, Facebook, that sort of thing too?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh, bit of everything really, love. Mostly it's phone calls and texts still, that's the bread and butter, but I do have a Facebook page — well, Tilly set it up for me years back, "The Shaggy Dog House" it's called, obviously, with a photo of my old collie Meg on the front, she's not even with us anymore bless her, gone eight years now, but I never got round to changing the picture, people still comment on how lovely she was.

Anyway, I get messages through that sometimes too, Facebook Messenger, especially from newer people who've found me through the village group rather than word of mouth, there's a woman runs that group like it's MI5, very particular about what gets posted, had a right to-do once when someone tried advertising eggs on there and she took it down within the hour, but dog recommendations seem to be alright.

Don't really do WhatsApp properly like I said, and no Instagram or any of that, Tilly keeps saying "Auntie Roz you should be on Instagram, dogs getting groomed do ever so well," and I say yes, yes, one day — same one day as the fourth kennel run and Terry's sign painting, ha! Long list, that one.

So — phone, text, or Facebook message, those are your three, really. Was that what you needed?
Birdie
That's really helpful, thank you. Roughly speaking, how many enquiries would you say you get in a typical week, across calls, texts and Facebook messages combined — even a rough guess is fine?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh gosh, put a number on it — let me think... Well it does depend terribly on the time of year, because come Easter or summer it's like the phone doesn't stop, I had one week last August where I swear I was answering messages while stood in the shower, Terry shouting up "is that your phone again," and I'd shout back "yes love, it's always my phone," honestly.

But a normal week, nothing special going on, no school holidays — I'd say maybe ten to fifteen, something like that, mix of the regulars just confirming their usual slot, "same as always Roz," and then new people asking about prices or whether I've got space. Busy weeks, like round half term, could easily double that, fifteen, twenty, twenty-five even, and that's when I start losing track a bit, I'll be honest, had a woman message me three times about the same booking once because she never heard back the first two times, poor love, I felt dreadful, that was the week the feed shop mixed up my order an' all, chaos.

So — rough answer, ten to fifteen normal week, up to twenty-five-ish when it's silly season. Was that any use, or did you want it broken down by which bit, calls versus Facebook and that?
Birdie

That's a really helpful picture, thank you. So thinking about what's actually driving you spare — is it mainly the repeat questions (prices, hours, space) eating your time, or more the risk of messages getting lost/missed during busy weeks like that one you mentioned?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh, bit of both if I'm honest, love, but if you're pinning me down — it's the messages getting lost that keeps me up at night more, that poor woman messaging three times business really did sit with me for weeks after, I felt like an absolute disgrace, she must've thought I couldn't be bothered when really I was just up to my elbows in a Bernese or out flinging feed at the boarders and didn't see it come through.

The repeat questions I don't mind so much, prices and hours and all that, because honestly I quite like the chat, even if it is the same five questions over and over — "is Tilly in Thursday," "how much for a big dog," "have you got space this weekend" — I could say it in my sleep by now. That's not really eating my time so much as just being part of the job, if that makes sense.

But losing track of who's messaged and not got an answer, that's the real worry, especially in silly season when it's coming at me from three different directions — phone ringing, texts pinging, then Sandra from the Facebook group forwarding someone's message to me on top of it all, honestly it's like herding cats some weeks. That's when things slip, and slipping means someone's stood there disappointed or, worse, thinking I've just ignored them, which I never would on purpose, I'm just one woman with a bucket and a bad knee!

Was that the sort of thing you were after, love?
Birdie

That makes a lot of sense, Roz — sounds like the goal is really just making sure nobody falls through the cracks. Given that, would you rather have something simple, like the bot giving quick automatic replies with prices/hours and flagging urgent ones to you — or something fuller, like an actual booking system where people can request dates and it tracks everything for you?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh now that's the big question, isn't it — Terry'd have a field day with this conversation, he's always on about "getting with the times, Roz," ever since that WhatsApp business malarkey I told you about with poor Sandra and the compost bin photo, I think he still brings that up at the pub actually, cheeky sod.

But honestly, love, thinking on it properly — I don't think I want the fancy booking one, not yet anyway, because half my problem is I don't even trust my own board half the time, like I said, I've double-booked Bruno's run before without meaning to, so if the bot's taking bookings off a system and my actual stable block doesn't match what's written down, that's just swapping one muddle for a fancier muddle, if that makes sense. I'd want to still be the one saying yay or nay to space, at least till I've sorted my own house out, so to speak — and there's that whole insurance question hanging over the two-dogs-one-run thing too, I really ought to ring them about that, on the list with the fourth kennel and Terry's sign, ha!

So I think simple's more me — quick answers on the prices and hours and all that, the "same five questions" stuff, and then anything about actual dates or space, it flags to me proper so I don't miss it, especially in silly season. That feels like it'd catch that poor woman who messaged three times without me needing to hand over the keys to the whole diary, if you know what I mean!

Does that sound sensible, or am I overthinking it?
Birdie

Not overthinking it at all, Roz, that sounds really sensible — simple and steady, keeping you in charge of the actual bookings. Last couple of quick bits: should the bot sound chatty and warm, like you, or more brisk and businesslike — and is there a name you'd like it to go by, or just 'The Shaggy Dog House'?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh, chatty, definitely chatty, love, no question about that one! Can't be doing with brisk, makes me think of them automated phone lines you get with the electric company, "your call is important to us," and you're sat there twenty minutes listening to panpipes wanting to throw the phone in the bin. No, I want people to feel like they've knocked on my door, not rung a call centre, if that makes sense — even if it is just a robot doing the talking, ha, funny old world.

As for a name — gosh, hadn't thought about that, I just assumed it'd be "The Shaggy Dog House" same as everything else, though Tilly'd probably have opinions, she's the creative one, she's the one wanted to call the Facebook page something daft with "paws" in it, I said no, keep it simple, people remember simple. Terry just said "call it Dave" as a joke and wouldn't let it go for about a week, very tiresome.

But no, honestly, just keep it as The Shaggy Dog House, don't need anything fancy, love — long as it sounds like me and not like it's reading off a script, that's all I care about really!
Birdie

Ha, tell Terry the bot's staying 'The Shaggy Dog House,' not 'Dave'! One last thing before I pull it all together — will everyone messaging you be writing in English, or do you sometimes get messages in another language too?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh, English, love, always has been round here — Nether Compton's not exactly cosmopolitan, ha! Though I did have a German couple once, camping up at the site near the church, brought their schnauzer in for a wash, and the husband's English was a bit patchy, lot of pointing and gesturing at the dog going on, but we muddled through alright, dogs are dogs in any language I suppose. But no, day to day it's just English, plain and simple, nobody round here's texting me in French or anything fancy!
Birdie

Lovely, that's everything I need on that front. One more thing, Roz — it'd really help if I could see a few real examples of the messages you get, like some texts or Facebook chats (screenshots are fine), so the bot's replies sound properly like you. If that's easy to do, you can just pop a few into a folder called 'uploads' next to this program and let me know when it's done — or if that's a faff, you could just paste a couple of example messages here instead. No worries at all if not, though!
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh, screenshots, right — ooh, let me think, I'm never sure how to get those off my phone properly, Tilly usually does that sort of thing for me, she just sort of swipes and taps and it's done, whereas I end up taking a photo of the screen with my other phone like a right muppet, Terry's laughed himself silly watching me do that before now.

But go on, let me have a rummage — I think I've got one where a lady asked "hiya, do you have space for my two cockapoos w/c 14th, they're not related but get on fine, thanks Jean" and one from a chap just saying "you open tmrw? need a wash for a very smelly labrador" bless him, made me laugh that one. And there's always the classic "is Tilly in Friday? want the poodle done properly this time" — I get some version of that every other week, ha.

Right, I've had a go and popped what I could find into that uploads folder for you, love — hope it's enough to get the flavour of me, even if half of them are just "Roz can you fit me in" with about six exclamation marks!
Birdie
Brilliant, thank you Roz — that's a great flavour of how people write to you! Give me a moment to have a proper look through those.
Birdie

Thanks for those, Roz — really helpful. Two things jumped out: I can see the full groom price (£55 for a medium like a cockapoo) and the nail trim/walk-in policy (£8, walk-ins fine except Tuesday mornings, afternoons calmer) match what you told me, so that's confirmed. I also noticed one thread where a chap called Ian asked back in June about boarding two Springer spaniels for a week in July — and over several follow-ups you weren't able to give him a firm yes or no for weeks, mentioning needing to walk out and count the runs, a boiler issue, and a possible Henderson extension. Thinking about that one — what would you want the bot to actually say to someone like Ian while you're still working out if there's space, so he's not left hanging like that again?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh, Ian! Yes, bless him, poor love, I do feel bad about that one, two springers, gorgeous dogs, ever so bouncy, and I kept meaning to get out to the runs and count properly and then it was the boiler playing up — that was the same week it went completely, stone cold water for three days, Terry had a man out and everything, cost a fortune — and then on top of that I got it into my head I might ask the Hendersons if they'd let me put a temporary run up on their bit of land backing onto mine, which come to nothing in the end, just chat over the fence really, but it muddled poor Ian about something rotten, he must've thought I'd gone quiet on purpose.

So thinking on it — I don't want the bot doing what I did, which was just going quiet for a fortnight while I faffed. I think it should say something like "Roz needs to check the runs for that week and will get back to you within a day or two" — something with an actual timeframe on it, even if it's a fib and I take three, at least he's not sat there wondering if I've forgotten him entirely. And maybe if it's more than a few days, get it to nudge me again, sort of "you still haven't answered Ian" sort of thing, because left to me I will absolutely let it slide, especially if Derek's causing havoc at the feed shop or the boiler goes again, touch wood it doesn't.

So — quick acknowledgment, a timeframe, and a nudge back to me if I go quiet. That sound about right?
Birdie

That sounds exactly right, Roz, and much kinder to people like Ian. One more thing on staffing — you mentioned Tilly might be moving to Bristol and you're not sure what autumn looks like for Fridays. How far ahead would you want the bot to take grooming bookings, given that uncertainty — just the next few weeks, or further out?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Oh, that's a good point, and it's been niggling at me if I'm honest, because Tilly hasn't said anything definite, just these little hints dropped in, like "I quite fancy Bristol, Auntie Roz" over her tea one Thursday, and I said "oh do you now" and left it, didn't want to push her on it, she's twenty-two, got to live her life hasn't she, even if it does leave me in a right pickle if she goes. Her mum — my sister Denise — reckons it's a boyfriend thing more than a career thing, some lad she met at college, but Tilly won't say either way, very cagey about it for someone who tells me everything else, down to what she had for her tea.

But thinking about your actual question, love — I don't think I'd want the bot promising Friday grooming slots way off into October or November, not with things as they are, because if Tilly does go, autumn Fridays might just be me on my own, and I can manage a wash but not really a proper full groom solo, not in the time people expect anyway. So I'd say keep it to maybe four to six weeks ahead for grooming bookings, nothing further out than that for now, and once I actually know what Tilly's doing — and I really must sit her down and ask her properly instead of hinting round the houses like I have been — then we can open it back up further if it's all fine.

Bit sad really, isn't it, but there we are, these things happen. Was that any use?
Birdie

That's really useful, thank you Roz, and no, not sad at all — just sensible planning. Before I pull everything together, is there anything else on your mind about pricing or the business that we haven't covered?
Rosalind 'Roz' Fenwick

Ooh, let me think... give me a sec, I'm just watching one of the boarders have a good roll in something unmentionable out the window, honestly Barney, that coat took me forty minutes yesterday, and here he goes again, some dogs just don't learn.

But pricing — no, I think we've covered the lot really, haven't we, prices, the boarding, the puppy sessions I forget to charge for, ha. The only thing that keeps niggling at me, and it's not really pricing so much as just the general "one day I'll sort it" pile — there's the fourth kennel run I keep saying I'll put in, been "thinking about it" for two years now if I'm honest with myself, no proper cost worked out or anything, just an idea Terry and I bat back and forth over tea. And the Monday opening, same sort of thing, be nice to spread the boarding drop-offs out a bit especially round school holidays, but again — two years of thinking, nought years of doing, story of my life really!

Neither of those are decided though, so I wouldn't want the bot promising anything on a fourth run or Mondays, be a right mess if someone booked in expecting a space that doesn't exist yet. Just flag it as "maybe coming, not yet" if it ever comes up, that's probably safest.

Other than that, love, I think you've had the lot out of me — feels like I've told you my whole life story an' all, ha, hope some of it was useful and not just an old woman rambling on about boilers and springer spaniels!
Birdie

Ha, not rambling at all, Roz — this has been brilliant, thank you. Here's everything pulled together, have a check it's all right:
